title: Subgroups of GL_2
promptMarkdown:
Let $G=GL_2(\mathbb R)$ under matrix multiplication. For each of the following subsets decide, with proof, whether it is a subgroup of $G$. When it is not, name the condition that fails and give an explicit witness.

(a) The upper triangular matrices in $G$ (those with zero below the diagonal).
(b) $\{A\in G:\det A=\pm1\}$.
(c) The matrices in $G$ with integer entries.
(d) The matrices with integer entries and $\det A=\pm1$.
(e) For a fixed $B\in G$, the centraliser $C(B)=\{A\in G: AB=BA\}$.

(f) Now replace $\mathbb R$ by the field $\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$. Determine $|GL_2(\mathbb Z_2)|$ with proof, and show that $GL_2(\mathbb Z_2)$ is non-abelian by exhibiting two matrices that do not commute.
hintLadder: For a candidate subgroup check identity, closure and inverses (or use the one-step test $gh^{-1}\in H$). When a condition fails, a single explicit matrix is a proof.
For $2\times2$ matrices, $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{\det A}\begin{pmatrix} d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$. When are the entries of $A^{-1}$ integers?
If $AB=BA$, multiply both sides by $A^{-1}$ on the left and on the right to relate $A^{-1}$ and $B$.
Build an invertible matrix over $\mathbb Z_2$ column by column: how many choices for a nonzero first column, and then for a second column outside the span of the first?

criteria.criterion: (a), (b) and (e) shown to be subgroups with identity, closure and inverses each justified (triangular inverse is triangular; det is multiplicative and det(A^{-1}) = 1/det A; conjugation argument for the centraliser).

levels.label: met
levels.description: All three with every condition justified.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Conclusions right, some conditions asserted without reason.

criteria.criterion: (c) is not a subgroup: an explicit integer matrix in G whose inverse is not integral, with the failing condition (inverses) named.
(d) is a subgroup: closure via integer products and multiplicativity of det, inverses via the adjugate formula with det = ±1.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both closure and the adjugate argument.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Inverses asserted without the adjugate reasoning.

criteria.criterion: |GL_2(Z_2)| = 6 by counting ordered pairs of linearly independent columns (3 choices then 2), or an equivalent complete count.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Correct count with a complete argument.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Correct count by exhaustive listing without the structural reason, or reason without verifying all 16 matrices are accounted for.

criteria.criterion: Two explicit matrices over Z_2 whose products in both orders are computed and differ.

checkExamples.label: column count
checkExamples.text: Over Z_2 a matrix is invertible iff its columns are linearly independent: 3 choices of a nonzero first column and 2 choices of a second column outside its span, so |GL_2(Z_2)| = 3·2 = 6.

checkExamples.label: wrong count
checkExamples.text: GL_2(Z_2) consists of all 2x2 matrices with entries in Z_2 except the zero matrix, so it has 15 elements.
